misconceptions.description: Using the image filename or the word 'image' as alt text instead of describing the content
misconceptions.feedback: Alt text should describe what the image shows and why it matters, for example 'Bar chart: club membership rose from 20 to 55 over the year.'

misconceptions.description: Making text big and bold to look like a heading instead of using a real heading style or tag
misconceptions.trigger: learner styles a line as large bold text but does not use a heading level
misconceptions.feedback: Use real heading styles or tags (Heading 1, Heading 2, h1, h2). Screen readers and navigation rely on the structure, not the visual size.

misconceptions.description: Relying on color alone to signal meaning, such as marking required fields only in red
misconceptions.trigger: learner uses color as the only cue for status or importance
misconceptions.feedback: Pair color with a label, icon, or text so the meaning is clear to people who cannot distinguish the colors.

misconceptions.description: Treating accessibility as an optional final touch rather than part of the design
misconceptions.trigger: learner plans to 'add accessibility later' after the artifact is done
misconceptions.feedback: Build accessibility in as you go: headings, alt text, contrast, and captions are part of a correct artifact, not extra polish.
